summary: Slot 1 (one pool): run 5 with October's spawn sources off, so 10% of training starts are the map start and 90% come from the search's backward curriculum; PPO, the search and its cadence unchanged (85 flags, commit da7981e5). Run azr1b1_pool1 (from scratch 2026-11-09 20:48 UTC, RTX 4080, ~355k steps/s) FINISHED sidistic from the true start at 14.194B steps (5/9, 117.68 s): all 12 walls ON TIME, 1.72x run 5 in steps and 1.78x in total ticks; walls 1-8 level with run 5 (0.98-1.12x from the post-CP2 block on), CP6 1.28x, CP7 1.22x. Best eval 113.912 at 15.327B (7/9, 115.97 s). The cost of one pool: the greedy keeps losing the early map (the CP2 block, ~30%) whenever the curriculum's line moves on; a patience line ending AT the failure repaired it 6/6 times, lines ending past it never did. After the first finish it finishes in 63% of evals (mean 1.94/9, never 9/9) against run 5's 98% (4.91/9) over the same 65 evals, but faster (best 115.07 s vs run 5's 117.94 s). For the user's question: one pool alone works but is slower and less steady than the hybrid; run 5's other 75% of starts acted as a replay of the whole map (slot 2's same pool + a balanced tree finished at 0.88x run 5, with the same loss of steadiness). Next: one pool + --demo-whole-frac 0.5 (half the curriculum spread over the whole line; built and tested here).
